# An `#id` written inside a component that inlines must reach the element the
# page emitted. The lowering leaves that id on the node and names it in every
# updater it builds, while html emits the element as `$N` — so without a
# mapping the updater assigned to an identifier nothing declared, and the first
# click threw ReferenceError instead of patching anything.
#
# Two instances, because the second half of the same bug is that one user id
# names two elements: each instance's handler has to patch its own.

sngl generate --lang=none --platform=html --out=out app.sngl
exists out/index.html

# No bare `shown` survives: every write goes through an emitted element var.
! grep 'shown\.textContent' out/index.html

# The two instances hold separate state, and each patches a different element.
grep 'v__inst0' out/index.html
grep 'v__inst1' out/index.html

# The elements the page declared are the ones the handlers write to.
grep '\$0.textContent = String\(state.v__inst0\)' out/index.html
grep '\$1.textContent = String\(state.v__inst1\)' out/index.html

# Neither handler reaches the other instance's element.
! grep '\$1.textContent = String\(state.v__inst0\)' out/index.html
! grep '\$0.textContent = String\(state.v__inst1\)' out/index.html

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import app "sngl:app"

component holder(seed int) node {
    var v = seed
    hbox {
        text #shown(value=string(v))
        button(text="bump", @click { v += 1 })
    }
}

component main node {
    holder #p(seed=1)
    holder #q(seed=2)
}

app.window {
    main
}
